sol.section: Recommended exact spec diff; §§10/12.3 mixed-fat-object applicability
sol.problem: The proposal changes launch-estimate and certificate invocation contracts without stating how a mixed fat object uses them. INDEX's general assertion that no north-star capability is removed does not supply the module boundary, launch-shim responsibility or certificate inventory required by the standing mixed-fat-object check. This is an omission in the proposed repair, not a request to redesign the accepted launch ABI.
sol.fix: Add this paragraph to the recommended normative diff for §§10/12.3: “In a mixed fat object, native host code remains native. The host launch shim loads the selected marked ISA module and negotiates the token-alias binding feature with its runtime and scheduler. Execution derives token_aliases from the actual live handles supplied to that device invocation; tuple-based estimate and scheduling requests supply the partition explicitly. Alias-bearing schedules and certificate invocation records bind the selected module's object/closure identities and resolved device invocation, rather than treating the native host binary as one ISA object. Native entry points, argv/envp and unaffected host libc require no device token-alias entries; the alias-binding inventory covers the marked device closures and their invocations.”

codex.section: Recommended exact spec diff: partition ordering and no-token defaults; §§10.1/11/12.3

steps.claim: Only oracle_call has a separate tk operand. action_call has mutable, input, memory and classical-argument lists, with no primary token.

The proposal instead prepends a separate token for region requests, says every region without token arguments has [0], and requires executors to derive partitions from actual live handles. Its no-separate-token exception names only CC/R entries.

The published controlled-action fixture calls flip with no token operands. Its actual token list is empty, but the proposal's region default requires [0]. For an action with one token argument a, the same omission leaves no source rule deciding whether a hypothetical primary token aliases a, distinguishing [0,0] from [0,1].

Consequently, action invocation partitions cannot be derived consistently between source execution, estimation and certificate replay. The premise that every region invocation supplies a primary token is false; this affects mandatory binding arity and schedule matching.

codex.fix: In §§10.1/11/12.3 and both no-token defaults, state: “For an oracle invocation, list its separate invocation token first, followed by token-typed arguments in signature order. For an action, permutation action or CC/R entry, list only token-typed parameters in signature order. Budget fields do not create token identities. The separate budget token accepted by the estimation ABI contributes an identity slot only when the subject is an oracle.” Correct examples: a token-free oracle has [0]; token-free controlled and flip actions have []; an action receiving a,b has [0,0] for one shared identity and [0,1] for distinct identities. Alternatively, define an explicit action context-token mechanism and its runtime propagation, but I recommend omitting the nonexistent primary identity because this preserves §4.7 and source hashes.

codex.section: Release and route; mixed-fat-object standing check
codex.problem: The proposal changes launch support, invocation identity and certificate bindings, but neither it nor INDEX's publication section states how a native-host-plus-marked-device-modules fat object uses them. The general assertion that no North Star capability is removed does not supply the explicit mixed-object application required by the standing check.
codex.fix: Add to Release and route: “A mixed fat object retains its native host binary and carries ISA objects and device certificates for marked device modules and their linked device closure. These token partitions are scoped to invocations of a loaded device program, not to the whole native binary. The launch runtime derives entry partitions from valid device token handles and preserves equality through device calls; serialization records equality classes only. Native host-only functions need no device certificate, and this repair does not require moving host entry points, argv/envp or the native libc closure into an ISA object.”
